paper_citation: Robert H. Allen & Sally P. Stabler
host_system: Human adult feces (n=18, supplemental B12 intake <=25 ug/d)
assay_or_method: Hot KCN extraction + LC-MS corrinoid speciation (bulk wet feces)
metric_name: Total fecal corrinoids (cobalamin + analogues)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Bulk wet-feces total corrinoid pool (9.66e-4 mol/m^3) numerically matches 1.0e-3 mol/m^3 (0.97x), not unbound extracellular ligand
empirical_quote_or_context: Table 4 mean total corrinoids 1309 ng Cbl eq/g (~0.966 uM bulk); >98% non-cobalamin analogues (2-MeAde 60.6%, p-cresol 16.3%, Ade 12.5%, 2-MeS-Ade 5.5% in Table 4 vs 15.5% abstract typo). Free fraction not measured.

paper_citation: Robert H. Allen & Sally P. Stabler
host_system: Human adult feces (n=18, supplemental B12 intake <=25 ug/d)
assay_or_method: Hot KCN extraction + LC-MS corrinoid speciation (Table 4 direct mean)
metric_name: Tabulated bulk cobalamin mean (Table 4: 19 ng/g; 1.4% of total)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Bulk cobalamin 71.3x below shipped 1.0e-3 mol/m^3 (0.0140x); cobinamide 1.8%; intracellular vs bound vs free unfractionated
empirical_quote_or_context: Table 4 reports 19 ng/g cobalamin directly (1.40e-5 mol/m^3); Allen & Stabler did not separate intracellular, protein-bound, or unbound extracellular pools.

host_system: C57BL/6 mice (cecal vs fecal)
assay_or_method: Heat/KCN homogenate extraction + LC-MS active cobalamin & corrinoids
metric_name: Bulk active B12 (Results & Fig. 1e mass-normalized ng/mg)
raw_unit: ng/mg (Results/Fig 1e; abstract misprints fecal as ng/ml)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Bulk baseline 16.9x (cecal) to 22.6x (fecal) below 1.0e-3 mol/m^3; oral supp (3.94 ug/mL water) raises bulk fecal B12 to 5.76e-3 mol/m^3 (5.76x above 1.0e-3)
empirical_quote_or_context: Results & Fig. 1e report ng/mg for both cecal (0.08 -> 10.60 ng/mg) and fecal (0.06 -> 7.81 ng/mg, 136-fold source-reported); abstract ng/ml is an internal unit error. Bulk extract does not measure free B12.

host_system: C3H/HeOuJ mice (naive & C. rodentium)
assay_or_method: Proprietary extraction buffer homogenate B12 assay (Fig. 1a + text)
metric_name: Homogenate cobalamin baseline vs 40 ug/mL CNCbl drinking water
raw_value: ~0.01 colon (~0.014 cecum) base; ~15 narrative (11-12 Fig) supp
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Bulk homogenate baseline ~135x below 1.0e-3 mol/m^3; tested high-dose water raised assayed B12 ~1000-fold to ~1.11e-2 mol/m^3 (single dose, not minimum threshold)
empirical_quote_or_context: Drinking-water CNCbl (~40 ug/mL) raised homogenate B12 from ~0.01 ppm (~7.38 nM bulk, rho=1 assumed) to ~11-15 ppm (~8-11 uM); does not isolate free interstitial CNCbl.

host_system: Healthy human donors (n=8) & MacFarlane batch ferm.
assay_or_method: UHPLC-DAD fecal/fermentation B12 + EIA starting medium T0
metric_name: Unspeciated fecal B12 (7/8 >LOD) & T0 medium (added vs EIA total)
raw_value: 2716 fecal med (684-4222); 5 added (EIA T0: 8.9 Control, 4.1 NB12)
gutibm_value: 2.00e-03 fecal; 6.57e-06 Control T0 (3.03e-06 NB12 T0; 3.69e-06 added)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Unspeciated fecal median 2.00e-3 mol/m^3 (D1 <30 ng/mL UHPLC LOD); assayed T0 medium is 6.57e-6 (with vitamin mix) or 3.03e-6 mol/m^3 (without added B12)
empirical_quote_or_context: At T24, 5/8 donor batch fermentations (D3, D5-D8; Control intracell 83+/-9 to 201+/-15 ng/mL) had intracellular > supernatant B12 and 3/8 had the opposite; NB12 T24 reached 152-564 ng/mL (1.12e-4..4.16e-4 mol/m^3; minor abstract vs Results SD discrepancy).

host_system: Human fecal (reusing Allen n=18 data) & bovine rumen/GI
metric_name: Corrinoid/cobamide richness & Simpson index
raw_value: Human: 8 corrinoids (7 cobamides), Simpson 0.41; Cow: 7 corrinoids, 0.23-0.35
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Human profile reuses Allen 2008; dominant [2-MeAde]Cba and analogue BtuB Kd values and free fractions remain unmeasured parameters
empirical_quote_or_context: Human average contains 8 corrinoids (7 complete cobamides plus cobinamide, Simpson sum-of-squares 0.41; narrative ~0.3 across mammals). Does not measure BtuB Kd or free fraction.

host_system: Living mouse GI lumen (He et al. 1999 EPR data cited in review)
assay_or_method: Noninvasive charcoal EPR oximetry synthesis (Konjar review citing He 1999)
metric_name: Stomach -> duodenum -> mid-SI/mid-colon slice -> distal/sigmoid lumen pO2
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Intraluminal mouse EPR values (3.93e-3 and 1.44e-2 mol/m^3) exceed 55e-6 by 71x-262x, but measure lumen/mixed slice rather than epithelial source tissue
empirical_quote_or_context: 3 and 11 Torr come from He et al. (1999) mouse intraluminal charcoal EPR (11 Torr slice includes mid-SI and mid-colon; Albenberg 2014 notes potential fecal EPR calibration bias).

host_system: Mouse distal colon ex vivo (top 50-60 um epithelial tissue; 2016 online / 2017 issue)
assay_or_method: Ex vivo phosphorescence lifetime imaging (PLIM, 3 h probe loading, inverted supply)
metric_name: Normal mucosal tissue oxygenation range
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Ex vivo intracellular epithelial range (5.0e-3..3.5e-2 mol/m^3) is 91x-636x above 55e-6, but reflects excised inverted-supply tissue rather than in vivo apical mucus
empirical_quote_or_context: Predominantly intracellular epithelial oxygenation in excised mouse distal colon (5-35 uM, paired with 4-28 Torr via study calibration); requires boundary transfer model for in vivo mucus.

host_system: Mouse cecal serosal/mucosal tissue vs cecal lumen
metric_name: Mouse intestinal tissue (~40 mmHg) vs censored intraluminal (<1 mmHg) pO2
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Confirms 1000x unit mismatch vs ~40-42 mmHg tissue (~5.2e-2..5.5e-2 mol/m^3) while showing cecal lumen is censored <1 mmHg (<1.31e-3 mol/m^3)
empirical_quote_or_context: Phosphorescence quenching recorded ~40 mmHg in mouse cecal tissue vs <1 mmHg upper bound in lumen (human rectal biopsy arm profiled microbiota rather than direct human O2).

host_system: Primary human colonic epithelium + anaerobes
assay_or_method: Integrated optical O2 sensor in microfluidic human colon-on-chip
metric_name: Engineered gas-equivalent luminal vs basal % O2 (plus cited 0.1-1 mmHg context)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Engineered chip sustained 0.8% luminal (7.96e-3 mol/m^3 at 1 atm dry; pre-deoxygenated medium 0.07+/-0.02%) vs 11.1% basal (0.110 mol/m^3); 0.1-1 mmHg is cited background
empirical_quote_or_context: Gas-equivalent O2 percentages (distinct from % air saturation) in an in vitro co-culture platform; does not measure native human mucosal boundary concentration.

host_system: Post-euthanasia mouse lumen + CRC histology/device reconstruction (bioRxiv preprint)
metric_name: Radial intestinal oxygen slope
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Preprint gradient estimate (0.01-0.06 mol/m^3/mm); multiplying by assumed 200-500 um mucus thickness is a linear model extrapolation, not a native healthy-mucus endpoint
empirical_quote_or_context: Combines post-euthanasia mouse electrode profiles, human colorectal-cancer histology/literature reconstruction, and device assays; treat as qualitative radial-gradient support.

host_system: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (aer) & BW25113 (anaer)
metric_name: Cross-study ATP maintenance comparison (Taymaz-Nikerel 2010 aer vs Gonzalez 2017 anaer)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Unpaired cross-strain/method ratio 0.72 (2.20 vs 3.05 mmol ATP/gDW/h at 24.56 g/C-mol); Taymaz-Nikerel co-estimated P/O=1.49+/-0.26 and Gonzalez used finite-growth residual
empirical_quote_or_context: Shows literature anaerobic ATP residual in BW25113 (0.054) is not higher than aerobic MG1655 intercept (0.075+/-0.015), though not a paired single-strain O2-switch assay.

host_system: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (aer, D=0.049) vs GJT001 (anaer, D=0.1)
metric_name: Unmatched total specific glucose uptake q_Glc ratio (D=0.10 LB+Glc vs D=0.049 minimal)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: 4.61x compares total q_Glc = mu/Y_G + m_S across different growth rates (0.10 vs 0.049 h^-1), strains (GJT001 vs MG1655), and media, so it does not isolate nongrowth maintenance
empirical_quote_or_context: Table 3: anaerobic GJT001 in LB+Glc (D=0.1 h^-1, Y=0.156 g/g) q_Glc=3.55 vs aerobic MG1655 minimal (D=0.049 h^-1, Y=0.426 g/g) q_Glc=0.77 mmol/gCDW/h.

host_system: E. coli K-12 MG1655 anaerobic glucose WT (n=3)
assay_or_method: Anaerobic bioreactor exchange rates + FBA-inferred ATPM flux (Table 1)
metric_name: FBA-inferred anaerobic nongrowth ATP maintenance r_ATPM (no aerobic arm)
conversion_formula: FBA max-ATPM fit; arrested r_ATPM/r_Glc = 4.16 / 1.90 = 2.19 ATP/Glc
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Provides anaerobic-only FBA r_ATPM (4.41+/-0.54 growing; 4.16+/-0.27 arrested at r_Glc=1.90+/-0.11 mmol/gDW/h -> 2.19 ATP/Glc), without an aerobic comparator
empirical_quote_or_context: r_ATPM is model-inferred via FBA consistency optimization rather than a direct zero-growth calorimetric measurement; constrains anaerobic ATP yield near ~2.2-2.8 ATP/Glc.

host_system: E. coli aerobic respiratory chain
metric_name: Effective respiratory P/O stoichiometry (mol ATP per O atom / 2e-)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Conditional stoichiometric scenario gives 3.36-5.76x (if m_ATP ratio=0.72) or 4.67-8.00x (if m_ATP equal) vs PARAMETERS.md 30/2=15.0 ceiling; not a direct paired zero-growth assay
empirical_quote_or_context: Proteomics/kcat-constrained modeling plus experiment places E. coli P/O at 1.0-1.5 ATP per O atom (1.01-1.07 at mu_max), below the textbook ~30 ATP/Glc ceiling in PARAMETERS.md:531.

paper_citation: Walter P. Hempfling & Stanley E. Mainzer
host_system: E. coli B (glucose-limited chemostat)
metric_name: Aerobic m_o vs anaerobic m_ATP
gutibm_value: P/O=1.5..2 -> m_ATP_aer=1.35..1.8; strain B m_ATP ~4x higher than K-12
conversion_formula: 1 mg-atom O = 1 mmol O atoms; 0.9 * P/O[1.5..2] = 1.35..1.8 mmol oxidative ATP/gDW/h (excludes SLP)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Historical E. coli B chemostat (m_o=0.9 mg-atoms O/gDW/h oxidative-only; anaerobic m_ATP=18.9 mmol ATP/gDW/h); distinct strain/accounting convention, not a K-12 bound
empirical_quote_or_context: Oxidative m_o excludes substrate-level ATP unless added separately; illustrates strong strain and method sensitivity of maintenance estimates.

host_system: E. coli W3110
metric_name: Enzymatic max glucose uptake capacity (aer vs anaer), FBA NGAM & GAM
raw_value: q_max: 10.5 aer vs 18.5 anaer; NGAM=7.6; GAM=13
raw_unit: mmol Glc/gDW/h; mmol ATP/gDW/h; mmol ATP/gDW
gutibm_value: NGAM=7.6 mmol ATP/gDW/h (PARAMETERS.md anchor); q_max ratio=1.76x
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Supplies W3110 NGAM=7.6 mmol ATP/gDW/h used in PARAMETERS.md:530 (note 0.524 gDW/g max yield is in Varma & Palsson 1993 at 30 C; 1994 Fig. 2 batch yield is 0.356 gDW/g); q_max ratio 1.76x is not maintenance
empirical_quote_or_context: Separates max uptake capacity (10.5 vs 18.5 mmol Glc/gDW/h), nongrowth ATP demand (7.6 mmol ATP/gDW/h), and growth-associated demand (13 mmol ATP/gDW).

host_system: Human healthy adults (n=50)
metric_name: Colonic transit time (CTT) & whole-gut (WGTT)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: 30.0 h e-folding sum sits within human capsule CTT range (2.1-63.5 h) and is 2.21x healthy capsule median (13.6 h); capsule CTT != bacterial washout dilution rate
empirical_quote_or_context: Median GET=4.8 h, SBT=5.1 h, CTT=13.6 h, WGTT=23.3 h; 32.3%/32.6%/35.4% (sum 100.3%) is an imposed prior temporal split, not an independent anatomical measurement.

host_system: Human healthy adults (22 ingestible capsule studies)
metric_name: Ranges of study-level central estimates: CTT (9 studies) & WGTT (11 studies)
conversion_formula: Direct hours (IC vs ROM upper ~50-70 h)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: 30.0 h is 3.8% above the upper range of capsule study central estimates (15.9-28.9 h) and near lower radiopaque-marker norms (~30-70 h)
empirical_quote_or_context: Reports ranges across study central estimates (not pooled meta-analytic medians): GET 0.4-15.3 h, SITT 3.3-7.0 h, CTT 15.9-28.9 h, WGTT 23.0-37.4 h.

host_system: Human healthy adults (n=111; 2019 online / 2020 issue)
metric_name: Segmental colonic fraction (Asc / Trans / Desc / Rectosig)
gutibm_value: Equal-sex 20h illustration: 6.50/5.90/3.10/4.50 h (32.5/29.5/38.0% if Desc+Rectosig grouped)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Female transverse (34%) exceeds ascending (32%); mapping to 12/8/10 h (40/26.7/33.3%) depends on anatomical grouping of cecum/ascending and descending/rectosigmoid
empirical_quote_or_context: 3D-Transit regional % of CTT (F: 32/34/17/17%, M: 33/25/14/28%); sample-weighted 20 h illustration is 6.50/5.94/3.11/4.45 h (illustrative calculation, not observed medians).

host_system: Piglets (TopigsNorsvin x Pietrain; n=10 anatomical, n=5 transit-timed)
assay_or_method: Oral marker to first green stool (2/5 timed pigs had loose stool)
metric_name: Time to first green stool appearance (n=5)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: 12.75+/-1.70 h is whole-gut first-stool appearance in n=5 piglets (2.35x numerically below 30 h), not a regional colonic residence mean
empirical_quote_or_context: Microbiota/pH profiled in n=10 piglets; transit timing to first green feces reported in n=5 (including 2 with loose stool).

host_system: Landrace pigs (fed/fasted; 2020 online / 2021 vol. 156)
metric_name: Small intestinal (SITT) & gastric emptying (GET)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Assay warning only: rigid SmartPill capsules suffer 20-264 h gastric retention in pigs and do not calibrate 30 h colonic residence
empirical_quote_or_context: SITT is 2.3-4.0 h, but non-digestible capsule trapping in the porcine stomach precludes using capsule WGTT as physiological digesta transit.

host_system: Young pigs (piglets)
metric_name: Oral-rectal dye appearance (first vs last) & two solid-marker cohort medians
gutibm_value: Fluid dye: 13.2 h first, 24.1 h last; Solid ROM cohort medians: 25.2 h, 48.9 h
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Whole-gut oral-rectal endpoints across distinct marker phases and cohorts; does not establish a uniform 2x fluid/solid ratio or regional colon tau
empirical_quote_or_context: Blue dye first stool 13.2 h (10.2-18.1), last stool 24.1 h (22.4-40.3); solid radiopaque marker medians 25.2 h and 48.9 h in separate piglet groups.

journal: Neuromodulation Technology at the Neural Interface
host_system: Young pigs
metric_name: Oral-rectal WGTT (prestimulation vs stimulation) & post-gastric bowel+rectum
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Post-gastric bowel+rectum (5-53 h) includes small intestine and cannot be equated to large-bowel-only residence
empirical_quote_or_context: Abstract-verified Neuromodulation study in young pigs: prestimulation WGTT medians 28.4/23.0 h, stimulation-week medians 23.0/19.8 h; bowel+rectum includes SI.

host_system: Growing pigs (30-85 kg, cannulated)
metric_name: Cumulative arrival / time-to-peak at mid-colon & rectal arrival
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Cumulative time-to-peak arrival from mouth to mid-colon/rectum in growing pigs, not isolated colonic segment residence tau
empirical_quote_or_context: Cannulated 30-85 kg pigs across NSP fiber diets; arrival times include gastric + SI + cecal passage and cannot be subtracted across unpaired diet endpoints.

host_system: CFP/Yit vs ICR mice primary (C57BL/6, BALB/c, C3H, DBA/2J cited from literature)
metric_name: Primary CFP vs ICR WGTT + secondary strain WGTT/distal-colon/MRT citations
raw_value: CFP WGTT 2.5x ICR (some >11 h); cited WGTT 2-6, C3H distal <3, DBA/2J MRT 10.3
gutibm_value: Cited WGTT 2-6 h (strain-dependent up to >11 h)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Shows rapid but strongly strain-dependent murine transit; whole-gut carmine arrival (2-6 h) does not directly identify a 1-3 h colonic e-folding mean
empirical_quote_or_context: Primary experiment found CFP/Yit median WGTT 2.5x longer than ICR (some >11 h); C57BL/6, BALB/c, C3H, and DBA/2J (10.3 h whole-gut MRT) values are secondary citations.

host_system: Mice (in vivo SPECT imaging)
metric_name: Qualitative 99mTc-DTPA imaging landmarks (stomach/SI -> cecum -> colon/rectum)
raw_value: Abstract 1h vs body 3h cecal labeling; colon/rectum labeled by 6-8h
gutibm_value: 3-5 h informal landmark interval (not calibrated residence tau)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Radiotracer reached/labeled colon and rectum by 6-8 h (not full clearance); subtracting 3 h from 6-8 h gives only an informal landmark gap, not regional mean residence
empirical_quote_or_context: Coarse SPECT timeline has internal abstract (1 h cecum) vs body (3 h widespread SI/cecum) timing difference and does not fit compartmental washout constants.

host_system: Conventional & germ-free mice
metric_name: Expected protocol timing to first carmine-red fecal pellet (conventional vs GF)
gutibm_value: 2-8 h protocol expectation to first red pellet (clearance can take >24 h)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Protocol benchmark for first-pellet leading-edge transit (faster in conventional than germ-free mice), not a population distribution of colonic residence means
empirical_quote_or_context: STAR Protocols guide notes typical 2-8 h window to first red pellet while full dye clearance can exceed 1 day.

host_system: Australian mammals (carnivores vs herbivores/omnivores)
assay_or_method: Cross-host fecal E. coli survey + well-mixed/flow Lotka-Volterra model
metric_name: Colicin producer frequency vs gut turnover rate
gutibm_value: High turnover (short transit) selects against colicinogeny
conversion_formula: Higher dilution/turnover raises invasion threshold in mass-action flow model
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Supports cross-host association (lower colicinogeny in rapid-transit carnivores, confounded by diet/guild) and turnover model; mucus/crypt toxin rescue is a separate GutIBM hypothesis
empirical_quote_or_context: Barnes, Sidhu & Gordon (2007) model collapses killing into pairwise interaction without explicit free-toxin advection, mucus retardation, or crypt geometry.

host_system: In vitro engineered E. coli batch culture (+/- 4% sorbitol; no mouse experiments)
assay_or_method: Ecological invasion theory (Thms 1-2) + 72h in vitro batch competition (invader at +8h)
metric_name: Rare-invader establishment into resident equilibrium (+/- private carbon source)
raw_value: 0% exclusion by toxin alone; 72h exclusion w/ private nutrient
gutibm_value: Rare invader needs positive initial net growth > dilution (private nutrient sufficient)
conversion_formula: Invader fitness = private carbon niche + interference toxin
discrepancy_vs_baseline: In vitro rare-invader theorem: infinitesimal weapon production cannot rescue negative initial invader growth; private nutrient is sufficient in vitro, not a universal exclusion requirement at high dose
empirical_quote_or_context: Engineered E. coli competition with 4% sorbitol vs delta-srlAEB resident was performed in vitro (Salmonella appears only as Discussion context).

host_system: E. coli pColE2 microfluidic & batch cultures
assay_or_method: Flow cytometry (pColE2 E2crimson reporter) + single-cell time-lapse lysis microscopy
metric_name: Operon expression fraction vs conditional lysis of induced cells (5h LB vs 24h M9-Glc)
raw_value: M9-Glc: 22-50% reporter+, 1% of induced lyse by 24h (n=548); LB: 1.6-26% reporter+, 44%/15% lyse by 5h (n=815)
gutibm_value: Conditional lysis fraction of induced cells (0.01/24h M9 vs 0.15-0.44/5h LB)
conversion_formula: Direct fraction; M9-Glc lysis within 24h vs LB 2-5h
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Demonstrates CsrA/nutrient post-transcriptional lysis gating, but conditional 5h/24h lysis fractions among induced cells do not map directly to per-division sos_lysis_prob
empirical_quote_or_context: Uses E2crimson transcriptional/translational reporters (not GFP); unequal observation windows (5 h LB vs 24 h M9-Glc) require explicit induction + delay modeling.

host_system: E. coli ColE2 (CWT, CAMP, CREP1/2) +/- MitC
metric_name: Post-MitC lysis time (70/85 vs 120/150 min), cea-cel delay (6 vs 19 min), & 48h 1:100 assay
raw_value: 70/85 min (CREP1/2) & 120/150 min (CAMP gly/glc) post-MitC; cea-cel 6 vs 19 min; R^2=0.89
gutibm_value: 4200-9000 s post-MitC lysis; 360 vs 1140 s cea-cel delay; C usually outcompeted by 48h at 1:100 (0 MitC)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Times are Construct/carbon-specific post-MitC addition (distinct from 6 vs 19 min CREP1/2 cea-cel delay); without MitC at 1:100, C is usually outcompeted after 48 h depending on strain/carbon
empirical_quote_or_context: Toxin release correlates with post-MitC lysis time across constructs/media (R^2=0.89); does not define a single universal delay from spontaneous single-cell SOS onset.

host_system: E. coli BZB1011 ColE2 vs WT-GFP / ColA (24h)
assay_or_method: In vitro competition across starting ratios (n=6)
metric_name: 24h 1:100 M9 relative fitness w & 4h/20h reporter inhibition frequency thresholds
raw_value: ColE2 w=1.94+/-0.38 (24h 1:100 vs WT-GFP); WT thresholds >0.5% (E8), E2 mid, >2% (E7); vs ColA >1% (E2/E8), >10% (E7)
gutibm_value: ColE2 w=1.94+/-0.38 (dimensionless 24h ratio); >1% vs ColA-GFP, intermediate (0.5-2%) vs WT-GFP
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Dimensionless 24-h relative fitness w (not additive +0.33 decades/h) in M9 without added B12 sweep; 0.5% and >2% WT cutoffs belong specifically to E8 and E7 in 4h/20h survival assays
empirical_quote_or_context: ColE8 (6x E7 basal) w=2.61+/-0.80, ColE2 (4x E7 basal) w=1.94+/-0.38, ColE7 w=1.44+/-0.06; B12 receptor-shielding extrapolation is a separate model hypothesis.

journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
host_system: E. coli producer/filtrate + lattice RPS PDE
metric_name: 30-min 50% filtrate survival loss & discrete lattice RPS intermediate accumulation
gutibm_value: Assay net loss rate >2.84e-4 /s (unquantified [tox]); lattice optimum c* = p*dl*(1-u)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: -ln(0.60)/1800 = 2.84e-4 /s is an assay-specific net viable loss rate at unknown filtrate molarity (not microscopic k_kill); discrete-time lattice parameters (D=0.002, dl, u) are dimensionless
empirical_quote_or_context: Qualitatively supports producer competitive optimum at intermediate toxin accumulation/diffusion rather than calibrated physical diffusivity.

host_system: E. coli C-S-R triad on agar plates / flasks
assay_or_method: Serial replica-plated static agar vs Mixed Plate & Mixed Flask controls (>=66 gen)
metric_name: 3-strain coexistence outcome
raw_value: Coexistence >=66 gen on static plate; collapse on mixed plate and mixed flask
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Core in vitro spatial validation benchmark: local dispersal maintains all three strains whereas global mixing collapses diversity
empirical_quote_or_context: Replica-plated static plates preserved neighborhood structure (>=66 generations coexistence), whereas both Mixed Plate and Mixed Flask controls collapsed diversity.

paper_citation: Benjamin C Kirkup & Margaret A. Riley
host_system: Co-housed streptomycin-treated mice (3 mice/cage initialized 1 strain/mouse; 1% pellet CFU LOD)
metric_name: Cage-level non-transitive strain replacement & single-pellet dominance
raw_value: Cyclic C->S->R->C cage-level replacements; individual pellets usually 1 dominant strain (>1% LOD)
gutibm_value: Between-host / metapopulation cyclic turnover benchmark (with some cage fixations)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Operates at multi-host cage/pellet scale (mixed pellets rare above 1% CFU LOD; some cages lost diversity), supporting GAP-09 hierarchical censoring rather than within-patch mucosal coexistence
empirical_quote_or_context: Kirkup & Riley (2004, Nature 428) initialized 1 strain per mouse across 3-mouse cages and tracked fecal pellet dominance replacements.

host_system: Selected E. coli panel (from 1,768 fecal isolates) + dixenic mice (bioRxiv preprint)
metric_name: 6h in vitro exclusion vs 10d dixenic mouse coexistence (no significant in vivo phage-transfer effect)
raw_value: pEndo (E7/E9-related chimera): 6h in vitro exclusion + phage boost; 10d mouse coexistence (null phage delta vs control)
gutibm_value: 6h (21600 s) in vitro exclusion vs 10d (864000 s) mouse coexistence (mechanism unresolved in vivo)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Preprint toxin is an E7/E9-related endonuclease (not canonical ColE2); in vivo mouse phage titres and lysogenization did NOT differ significantly from bacteriocin-deletion controls
empirical_quote_or_context: Henrot, Debarbieux & Petit (2026 preprint): DNA-damaging E-type endonucleases + Mcc1229 induced prophages in vitro, but 10-d mouse coexistence was not shown to be caused by colicin-driven lysogenization.

host_system: Monoxenic germ-free mice (E. coli lambda: n=3 ODE fit; n=6 regression) vs LB plating
assay_or_method: In vivo L/S dynamics + ODE fit vs LB in vitro
metric_name: Mouse gut induction rate vs in vitro (and 0.8% bile salts)
discrepancy_vs_baseline: Monoxenic mouse E. coli lambda hazard (1.70e-6 to 4.44e-6 /s) is 9.7x-25.4x above Spec 14's 1.75e-7 /s; Table 2 in vitro 3.4e-4 is an infective-center fraction, not a unit-matched per-gen hazard
empirical_quote_or_context: Using binary generations/h = mu/ln(2) at mu=0.25 h^-1 gives 1.70e-6 /s (1.72e-6 via -ln(0.983)); confirms elevated monoxenic gut lambda reactivation without equating IC plating fraction to hazard.

host_system: Mouse gut evolved E. coli lysogens (d165-d493)
assay_or_method: Ex vivo LB + 5 ug/mL MitC optical-density lysis slope (steepest ln[OD(+MitC)/OD(-MitC)])
metric_name: Assay-defined max MitC OD600 lysis slope (early d104/new vs evolved d165/d493)
